St. Symeon Metaphrastes

St. Simeon Metaphrastes · St. Symeon the Metaphrast · St. Simeon the Metaphrast

Period
Tenth century; traditional Prologue dates his repose to about 960
Region
Constantinople
Titles / vocation
Writer · Monastic
Commemoration
November 9

Introduction

A Byzantine compiler of saints’ lives whose name also appears in Orthodox Communion prayers. He is distinct from Saint Symeon the New Theologian.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Repose, about 960 in the Prologue; no execution described

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The Prologue portrays St. Symeon as a learned Constantinopolitan who served at the imperial court before retiring from secular work. Its details belong to a received hagiographic account.

[1] Published Orthodox hagiography · Opening description

Life and notable events

His enduring work was the collection and literary revision of saints’ biographies. The OCA’s introductory catechesis places the beginning of his compilation in the tenth century and explains how such narratives are organized for liturgical remembrance.

[2] Official Orthodox life · Page 72, The Lives of the Saints

Death and martyrdom

The Prologue dates his repose to about 960 and reports myrrh associated with his body. It does not describe an execution. The approximate date is retained as that source’s chronology.

[1] Published Orthodox hagiography · Concluding sentence

Writings and legacy

The GOARCH Synekdemos includes a Communion preparation prayer under his name. Hagiography and prayer attribution explain why a learner encounters him in both saints’ lives and prayer books.

[3] Published Orthodox hagiography · Prayers in preparation for Holy Communion, Eighth Prayer: St. Symeon Metaphrastes

Chronology

  1. Tenth century

    Compilation of saints’ lives begins, in the OCA account.

    [2] Official Orthodox life · Page 72

  2. About 960

    Traditional repose date supplied by the Prologue.

    [1] Published Orthodox hagiography · Concluding sentence
